notes:
Stephen Zielinski & Anna are buried in Glen Eden Mem. Gardens on N.Main,Wpg. PlotLot 90, spaces B 1 & 2,  Gar.of Everlasting Life.On Nov.26/96.  Rose said in Olesko,they were Catholic and now that many LDS church records have been found, this has been confirmed.  The priest apparently told Stephen that no fee was req,d but after the marr.he demanded money & Stephen no longer went to Church.  In Canada he became a J.W.but soon gave that up.The JW org. attempted a law suit but abandoned it. Stephen was buried under the Lutheran rite. According to the 1915 issue of Henderson Guides, he worked as a tailor for D. Cameron and his residence is shown to be 708 Alfred Ave. He also worked for the HBC and then for 23 yrs at Eatons retiring in January, 1950. Rose said that initially,following immigration Stephen lived with Anton Landkammer .  The 1912 Henderson Guides show that address to be 685 Aberdeen.  By 1916, the Henderson guide no longer lists Anton as a resident of 685 Aberdeen, but it shows his brother John Landkammer living there and another brother George Landkammer lived at 711 Alfred Ave.  Copies of these Henderson Guides are on file in the Zielinski green book.
Refer to copy of LDS film # 2037645, Page 63.  This clearly shows parents as Andreas Zielinski and Catherine Grabowska and grandparents of Stephen as Antoni Zielinski + Pelagia Kowalska and, Nicolai Grabowski + Annae Hryniewicz.This record also shows that Stephens birthdate was December 20 and not December 14 as indicated by his hand in his Bible.Refer to copy of LDS film # 2037644, Page 8, which records the marriage of Stephen Zielinski and Anna Landkammer on June 9, 1908 and not June 14, 1908 as written in Stephen's bible.  It may be the Julian/Gregorian differential.
